title: Committee of Supply debate on the Ministry of Trade and Industry budget
what_it_is: A Committee of Supply debate on Head V of the Ministry of Trade and Industry's budget, opened by a proposed $100 reduction and followed by Members' cuts and ministerial responses.
why_it_matters: The debate covers MTI's budget and policy directions, including support for SMEs, internationalisation, energy, and consumer protection. It records that public consultations on consumer protection will begin on 16 March 2026, and that the Government will reassess GDP and inflation forecasts if necessary. The record does not state that the specific proposals raised by Members were adopted.

key_points.point: Moved a $100 reduction to Head V of the Estimates for the Ministry of Trade and Industry.
key_points.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
key_points.quote: That the total sum to be allocated for Head V of the Estimates be reduced by $100

key_points.point: Asked whether more targeted AI diffusion support for SMEs could be tied to measurable outcomes.
key_points.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
key_points.quote: can we design more targeted AI diffusion support for small and medium enterprises (SMEs), tied to measurable outcomes such as productivity improvements, cost savings or new market access?

key_points.point: Asked whether a counter-cyclical accelerator could be pre-approved for quick activation during downturns.
key_points.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
key_points.quote: should we consider a counter-cyclical accelerator, pre-approved support that can be activated quickly during downturns

key_points.point: Asked for an update on the Tourism 2040 roadmap.
key_points.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
key_points.quote: Could the Minister provide an update on the Tourism 2040 roadmap?

key_points.point: Asked about progress on the Greater Sentosa Master Plan and its projected economic contribution and job creation.
key_points.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
key_points.quote: On the Greater Sentosa Master Plan, what progress can be made, and what is the projected economic contribution and job creation?

key_points.point: Asked for projected job creation numbers over the next five to 10 years and how they are distributed across skill levels.
key_points.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
key_points.quote: What are the projected job creation numbers over the next five to 10 years and how are these distributed across skill levels?

key_points.point: Asked how effective the Capability Transfer Programme has been in practice.
key_points.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
key_points.quote: How effective has the Capability Transfer Programme been in practice?

key_points.point: Suggested MTI set a target for new local companies to reach $1 billion in annual revenue by 2035.
key_points.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
key_points.quote: MTI could consider setting an ambitious target for a number of new local companies to reach that scale by 2035

key_points.point: Suggested a separate tier for companies between $100 million and $200 million in annual revenue with slightly lower support than the SME tier.
key_points.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
key_points.quote: MTI could consider adding a separate tier of companies between $100 and $200 million in annual revenue, with slightly lower support than the SME tier

key_points.point: Said Enterprise Financing Scheme support for domestic acquisitions up to $500 million in revenue lapses in a month.
key_points.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
key_points.quote: Currently, the Enterprise Financing Scheme supports domestic acquisitions undertaken by firms up to $500 million in revenue, but this support lapses in a month.

key_points.point: Called on the Government to grant CCS administrative enforcement powers for breaches of the CPFTA.
key_points.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
key_points.quote: I call on the Government to grant CCS similar administrative enforcement powers for breaches of the CPFTA.

key_points.point: Said consumers suffered over $2.7 million in prepayment losses in 2025, a 40.4% increase from 2024.
key_points.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
key_points.quote: In 2025, consumers suffered over $2.7 million in prepayment losses. This is a 40.4% increase from 2024.

key_points.point: Called for a mandatory cooling-off period for all businesses that collect significant prepayments.
key_points.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
key_points.quote: I therefore call on the Government to introduce a mandatory cooling-off period for all businesses that collect significant prepayments.

key_points.point: Said public consultations on consumer protection will begin on 16 March 2026.
key_points.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
key_points.quote: Public consultations will begin on 16 March 2026.

key_points.point: Said the CPFTA was not designed for the current commercial world and is falling short.
key_points.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
key_points.quote: The CPFTA was not designed for this world. It is falling short today and Singaporeans are paying the price.

key_points.point: Proposed that advertised prices for fixed-term subscriptions reflect the average cost across the full contract term.
key_points.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
key_points.quote: any advertised price for fixed-term subscription must reflect the average cost across the full contract term.

key_points.point: Proposed explicit active consent before any trial converts to a paid subscription.
key_points.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
key_points.quote: we should ask for explicit active consent before any trial converts to a paid subscription.

key_points.point: Proposed that if it is one click to sign up, it should be one click to cancel.
key_points.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
key_points.quote: If it is one click to sign up, it should be one click to cancel.

key_points.point: Proposed empowering CCS with direct administrative powers like the UK's Competition and Markets Authority, including fines up to 10% of global annual revenue.
key_points.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
key_points.quote: we should empower the CCS with direct administrative powers like the UK's Competition and Markets Authority, which can levy fines of up to 10% of global annual revenue for consumer law breaches without going to Court.

key_points.point: Invited MTI to consider working with the Ministry of Home Affairs and the Attorney-General's Chambers to examine criminalising severe predatory sales tactics directed at vulnerable people.
key_points.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
key_points.quote: I invite MTI to consider working with the Ministry of Home Affairs and the Attorney-General's Chambers to examine criminalising severe predatory sales tactics that are directed at vulnerable people.

key_points.point: Proposed special listing rules for technology ventures in the size of about $50 to $100 to 150 million.
key_points.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
key_points.quote: I believe that our exchange can be structured for special listing rules for the technology ventures in the size of about $50 to $100 to 150 million

key_points.point: Said micro and small enterprises employ 45% of workers but contribute only 11% of nominal value added.
key_points.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
key_points.quote: They employ 45% of our workers but contribute only 11% of nominal value added.

key_points.point: Asked whether the Government would adopt ASME's suggestion to delineate micro enterprises and SMEs in national policy-making and data collection.
key_points.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
key_points.quote: Would the Government adopt ASME's suggestion to delineate micro enterprises and SMEs in national policy-making and data collection?

key_points.point: Suggested integrating succession planning and family ownership transition as core components of SME transformation.
key_points.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
key_points.quote: I therefore suggest that our SME transformation framework integrate succession planning and family ownership transition as core components of enterprise upgrading.

key_points.point: Suggested an integrated AI assistant on Government portals to suggest relevant programmes and schemes automatically.
key_points.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
key_points.quote: could there be an integrated AI assistant that understand the firms' profiles and suggest relevant programmes and schemes automatically?

key_points.point: Said newer EVs require proprietary diagnostic software and independent workshops may lack authorised access or compatible systems.
key_points.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
key_points.quote: newer EVs require proprietary diagnostic software. Independent workshops may lack authorised access or compatible systems.

key_points.point: Suggested offering SMEs a year-long subscription to enterprise AI tools.
key_points.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
key_points.quote: One practical way to narrow this gap is to offer SMEs a year-long subscription to enterprise AI tools

key_points.point: Asked what specific gap the additional $1 billion injection into Startup SG Equity is trying to close.
key_points.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
key_points.quote: With the additional $1 billion injection into our Startup SG Equity, I would like to ask MTI what specific gap we are trying to close?

key_points.point: Said owners are consumed by rent, manpower, compliance and cashflow issues, leaving little bandwidth for transformation.
key_points.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
key_points.quote: First, bandwidth. Owners are consumed by rent, manpower, compliance and cashflow issues.

key_points.point: Asked whether support should more deliberately prioritise SMEs that are willing and able to scale.
key_points.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
key_points.quote: should we more deliberately prioritise SMEs that are willing and able, or potentially able, to scale, to innovate and uplift productivity meaningfully?

key_points.point: Said China is the second largest owner of retail businesses in Singapore, accounting for 3% of retail businesses, and the perception of displacement cannot be ignored.
key_points.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
key_points.quote: China is the second largest owner of retail businesses in Singapore. Even though Chinese owners account for only 3% of retail businesses, the perception of displacement cannot be ignored

key_points.point: Asked whether MTI could consider targeted measures such as rental relief schemes and tenancy support for heritage and neighbourhood retailers.
key_points.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
key_points.quote: Can the Ministry consider targeted measures, such as rental relief schemes, tenancy support for heritage and neighbourhood retailers

key_points.point: Said it is crucial for the Ministry to explore partnerships with other nations and develop additional Free Trade Agreements.
key_points.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
key_points.quote: it is crucial for the Ministry to explore potential partnerships with other nations and develop additional Free Trade Agreements (FTAs).

key_points.point: Suggested MTI develop GNP indicators to track value created globally by Singapore and Singaporeans overseas.
key_points.speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
key_points.quote: I suggest that MTI develops GNP indicators to track value created globally by Singapore and Singaporeans overseas.

key_points.point: Suggested positioning Singapore as the trusted gateway to the Johor-Singapore SEZ.
key_points.speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
key_points.quote: position Singapore as the trusted gateway to the SEZ.

key_points.point: Said Singapore's advantage is not about adopting AI but being the most trusted place to deploy AI.
key_points.speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
key_points.quote: Singapore's advantage is not about adopting AI but being the most trusted place to deploy AI.

key_points.point: Said four in five Singapore SMEs plan to expand overseas, but only 3.1% of the resident workforce has worked overseas full-time for at least six months.
key_points.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
key_points.quote: four in five Singapore SMEs plan to expand overseas. Yet only 3.1% of our resident workforce has worked overseas full-time for at least six months.

key_points.point: Asked whether MTI will expand the Global Ready Talent Programme or explore grants to co-fund Singaporeans' relocation costs within ASEAN.
key_points.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
key_points.quote: will MTI expand the Global Ready Talent Programme or explore grants to co-fund Singaporeans' relocation costs within ASEAN?

key_points.point: Asked whether MTI could differentiate internationalisation support by market risk profile, with enhanced working capital guarantees, political risk coverage or expanded risk-sharing mechanisms.
key_points.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
key_points.quote: Could MTI consider differentiating internationalisation support not only by firm size, but also by market risk profile, with enhanced working capital guarantees, political risk coverage or expanded risk-sharing mechanisms in higher-risk corridors?

key_points.point: Said consortium-led bids would allow complementary Singapore companies to pool capabilities, share risk and compete for projects none could secure alone.
key_points.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
key_points.quote: would allow complementary Singapore companies to pool capabilities, share risk and compete for projects none could secure alone.

key_points.point: Said about half of new firms do not survive beyond five years and fewer than 1% become unicorns.
key_points.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
key_points.quote: About half of new firms do not survive beyond five years. Fewer than 1% become unicorns.

key_points.point: Asked how pathways are being strengthened for Singaporeans to venture into entrepreneurship and return to employment without stigma or structural disadvantage.
key_points.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
key_points.quote: how are we strengthening pathways that allow Singaporeans – from fresh graduates to mid-career professionals – to venture into entrepreneurship and return to employment without stigma or structural disadvantage?

key_points.point: Asked how leadership, IP ownership and value creation can remain anchored in Singapore as companies scale globally.
key_points.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
key_points.quote: how do we ensure leadership, IP ownership and value creation remain anchored here

key_points.point: Said Singapore's economy grew by 5% last year, performing better than expected despite a challenging global environment.
key_points.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
key_points.quote: Last year, Singapore's economy grew by 5%, performing better than expected despite a challenging global environment.

key_points.point: Said the US Supreme Court struck down reciprocal tariffs and the US Administration replaced them with a new Section 122 tariff of 10% for up to 150 days.
key_points.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
key_points.quote: The United States (US) Supreme Court has struck down the reciprocal tariffs that were imposed last year and the US Administration has since replaced it with a new Section 122 tariff of 10% for up to 150 days.

key_points.point: Said the Strait of Hormuz has been closed.
key_points.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
key_points.quote: The Strait of Hormuz, which is a key shipping route for crude oil and liquefied natural gas (LNG), has been closed.

key_points.point: Said the Government is monitoring developments and will reassess GDP and inflation forecasts if necessary.
key_points.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
key_points.quote: We are monitoring the developments closely and will reassess our GDP and inflation forecasts if necessary.

key_points.point: Said the Government set up the Economic Strategy Review to reset Singapore's economic strategy.
key_points.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
key_points.quote: This is why the Government set up the Economic Strategy Review (ESR) to take a hard, honest look at how Singapore must reset our economic strategy.

key_points.point: Outlined five strategic thrusts, with MTI colleagues to elaborate later.
key_points.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
key_points.quote: Let me outline broadly five strategic thrusts and my colleagues in MTI will elaborate later.

key_points.point: Said Singapore is already a global node in advanced manufacturing sectors such as semiconductors, medical products, specialty chemicals and aerospace.
key_points.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
key_points.quote: Singapore is already a global node in advanced manufacturing sectors, such as semiconductors, medical products, specialty chemicals and aerospace

key_points.point: Said Singapore will develop as a global hub for trust-based services such as risk advisory, cybersecurity, AI assurance and Testing, Inspection and Certification.
key_points.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
key_points.quote: We will build on this to develop Singapore as a global hub for trust-based services, such as risk advisory, cybersecurity, AI assurance and Testing, Inspection and Certification.

key_points.point: Said Singapore must push the frontier into new areas of growth such as quantum, decarbonisation technologies and space-related industries.
key_points.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
key_points.quote: we must also push the frontier into new areas of growth, such as quantum, decarbonisation technologies and space-related industries.

key_points.point: Said the second thrust is to sustain a dynamic and vibrant enterprise ecosystem spanning multinational corporations, high-growth companies and a vibrant start-up community.
key_points.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
key_points.quote: Second, we must sustain a dynamic and vibrant enterprise ecosystem, spanning multinational corporations, high-growth companies and a vibrant start-up community.

key_points.point: Said the Government would be happy to facilitate a Singapore industrial estate in the Johor-Singapore SEZ if interested commercial parties are willing to invest.
key_points.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
key_points.quote: It is an interesting idea and we will be happy to facilitate if there are interested commercial parties that are willing to invest in this estate.

key_points.point: Said Singapore and Malaysia are exploring a Digital Nomad Pass.
key_points.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
key_points.quote: we are exploring a Digital Nomad Pass between the Singapore Government and the Malaysian government.

key_points.point: Said work has moved to FEED studies with a local conglomerate on ammonia.
key_points.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
key_points.quote: we have actually worked with a local conglomerate where we have moved on to do FEED studies

key_points.point: Said transportation of green hydrogen is very expensive and the logistics chains are not established yet.
key_points.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
key_points.quote: today, the transportation of green hydrogen is very, very, very expensive and logistically, today, the chains are not established yet.

key_points.point: Said the $800 million Decarbonisation Grand Challenge aims to crowd in big gencos, big MNCs and local SMEs.
key_points.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
key_points.quote: the $800 million Decarbonisation Grand Challenge, is something that we hope to be able to crowd in from the big gencos, the big MNCs, to our local SMEs

key_points.point: Said diversification and energy transition to lower carbon alternatives will come with costs.
key_points.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
key_points.quote: part of that diversification and energy transition resulting in lower carbon alternatives will come with costs.

key_points.point: Said carbon pricing reflects the true cost of that modality of energy generation.
key_points.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
key_points.quote: our carbon pricing is a reflection of the true cost of that particular modality of energy generation.

key_points.point: Said the Government convened an independent Consumer Protection Review Panel last year and it is on track to table its findings.
key_points.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
key_points.quote: the Government convened an independent Consumer Protection Review Panel last year. They are on track to table their findings to us.

key_points.point: Said the Government stands prepared to take a whole-of-Government view to enhance consumer protection and ensure enforcement agencies have the necessary capacity and teeth.
key_points.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
key_points.quote: we stand prepared to take a whole-of-Government view to enhance our consumer protection regime to do two things. One, to safeguard the emerging risk and also, to ensure that the enforcement agencies are given the necessary capacity and teeth to enforce.

key_points.point: Sought leave to withdraw the amendment.
key_points.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
key_points.quote: I seek leave to withdraw my amendment.

what_happens_next: Mr Saktiandi Supaat sought leave to withdraw his amendment; separately, public consultations on consumer protection will begin on 16 March 2026.
